title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
overview: A 30-credit Applied Artificial Intelligence major awarding a BA in Interdisciplinary Studies. The department emphasizes responsible AI workflows and professional project work. Major and full-degree requirements remain partially mapped.

outcomes.text: Frame open-ended problems, select AI tools, evaluate outputs, coordinate AI agents and communicate results. Build a portfolio demonstrating responsible professional AI use.

requirements.title: Major credit minimum
requirements.summary: The department describes a 30-credit undergraduate major. This is the major total, not the complete BA degree total.

requirements.title: Core courses named in residency policy
requirements.summary: The FAQ explicitly names these core courses. This is an incomplete inventory; DATA 305 conflicts with AAI 301 in the linked example pathway.

requirements.title: Transfer, AP and cross-department substitutions
requirements.summary: Substitutions require departmental review of the prior course and syllabus; curriculum committee approval may be required.

requirements.title: External-faculty independent research
requirements.summary: For DATA 490 with a faculty member outside Data Science, the faculty member submits a proposal of no more than one page describing goals, data, methods and the desired 3 or 4 credits. Curriculum committee approval is required.

requirements.title: Study abroad and residency
requirements.summary: Study-abroad credit requires departmental preapproval. The listed core courses should be taken at W&M, with rare exceptions requiring curriculum committee consent; the capstone must be completed at W&M.

requirements.title: Study-abroad equivalency
requirements.summary: Equivalent approved courses transfer under the corresponding W&M course number after faculty review. Relevant courses without a W&M equivalent may transfer as DATA 340 after faculty and curriculum committee review.

requirements.title: Arts & Sciences declaration
requirements.summary: Students already in Arts & Sciences may declare directly without a separate application to the School of Computing, Data Sciences & Physics.

requirements.title: Major declaration and advising
requirements.summary: Declare after 39–54 earned credit hours, including AP, IB and transfer credit. Request an advisor, review the major declaration with the advisor, and submit the signed form to the Registrar. Annual advisor check-ins are recommended.

requirements.title: Earned-credit declaration thresholds
requirements.summary: Major declaration is permitted at 39 earned credits and required at 54; in-progress credits do not count. Entrants with AP, IB or dual-enrollment credit may wait until 39 credits earned since high school; transfers entering with at least 54 credits may wait until the end of their first W&M semester.

requirements.title: Major declaration review and changes
requirements.summary: Use a What If degree audit and major worksheet; the student and major advisor must sign. Double majors submit separate forms. Major changes must be submitted before the last add/drop day of the final semester. Program-specific declaration instructions continue to apply.

requirements.title: Major, minor and degree relationship
requirements.summary: The form explicitly includes the School of Computing, Data Sciences and Physics: one major is required; students may have two majors or one major and a minor. W&M awards one baccalaureate degree based on the primary major; two majors do not constitute two degrees.

notes: Curriculum evidence reviewed on 2026-10-10. The official catalog returned a JavaScript/robot challenge; no access restriction was bypassed. Department sources support the observations below, but a full catalog audit remains outstanding.
Published credits remain in source units (unknown normalized unit). Course credit values, descriptions, prerequisites, syllabi and calendar have not been inferred.

The linked example pathway names AAI 101, AAI 301, AAI 302, DATA 201, DATA 405 and DATA 303, plus ethics and methods alternatives and two elective slots. These have not been promoted into a complete required-course inventory because the pathway is illustrative and conflicts with the FAQ on Designing AI Agents.
The example pathway lists DATA 202 or PHIL 150 for ethics; its methods and elective options are explicitly examples, so they are not treated as exhaustive approved pools.

Printed month-only revisions are retained in source locators; no day or effective catalog year is invented. The known catalog challenge was not retried. PDF text is manually reviewed evidence, not supported by the ordinary text-only HTTP scrape path.
